what_happened: Re-verified .opencode_OLD/ as a strict subset of live .opencode/ (diff -rq: 38 differing entries, all additions/updates in the live tree, zero entries unique to _OLD) and deleted it, reclaiming 62 MB. Confirmed both .opencode_OLD/ and data/ are gitignored with zero tracked files (git ls-files empty for both), so the deletion produced no commit.

Dispatch description names the smaller abandoned checkpoint as '.checkpoint.partial' (15 MB); the actual file on disk is data/bmlogic-c8-clean.checkpoint.partial (15,343,086 bytes), sharing the bmlogic-c8-clean lineage with the 375 MB .jsonl.partial and its metadata sidecar. Sizes match exactly; this is a filename-in-prose drift, not a wrong-file risk.

Carried-figure re-validation caught a stale dispatch premise: the description's Item 1 instructs the plan to delete .opencode_OLD/, but a live 'ls -d .opencode_OLD' showed it was already removed during the research dispatch. Planning that phase from the description alone would have produced a work item with nothing to do. All other carried figures (two .partial byte counts, .gitignore:105/:107, zero tracked files under data/, proof_steps.jsonl at 1,650,583,836 bytes) re-confirmed unchanged against live disk.
